tokyo_marugoto_vegan_dining_as.price_note: ⚠ NO DISHES OR PRICES — the menu is published as hashed PNG images with no alt text, so not one item name is readable. That is genuinely frustrating here, because THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT RESTAURANT IN THE TOKYO SET FOR BOTH DIETS AT ONCE and the shop documents its own policy in more detail than any other record in this dataset. What follows is that policy, quoted, and it is worth more than a dish list. Tabelog not consulted: it has served Cf-Mitigated: challenge (HTTP 403) to this egress since 2026-09-02. ⚠ THE CLAIM: the shop states 「店内提供料理及び、店内販売商品は全てグルテンを使用していない食品です」 — every dish served in the restaurant and every product sold in it is made without gluten — and the site header carries 全料理メニューグルテンフリー(小麦不使用). It is simultaneously an all-plant kitchen: 「全てのお料理に、アルコール及び豚肉の使用はございません」, and 五葷 (garlic, spring onion, onion, nira, rakkyo) are excluded from EVERY dine-in dish, which is the Buddhist 精進 standard and goes further than veganism does. A restaurant that is vegan, wheat-free and allium-free by policy is close to unique. ⚠ AND THE SHOP ITSELF REFUSES THE STRONGER CLAIM, WHICH IS WHY THIS RECORD IS "high" AND NOT "dedicated": 「完全にグルテンフリー対応のレストランとして運営しているわけではないため」 — we are NOT operated as a fully gluten-free restaurant. The specific gap they name is the honest one: 「製造時に工場でのコンタミネーションの有無については、確認していません」 — for bought-in seasonings and sauces they have NOT verified whether cross-contamination occurred at the factory. So the recipes contain no wheat; the supply chain is unaudited. That is exactly the distinction between an ingredient statement and a safety guarantee that RAKERU’s allergen page also drew, and this shop draws it voluntarily and in the customer’s favour. ⚠ TWO CARVE-OUTS THAT MATTER AND ARE EASY TO MISS. First: BEER. The menu page states 「ビール・ノンアルコールビールは小麦の使用あり」 — the beer AND the non-alcoholic beer contain WHEAT. In a restaurant where a coeliac can safely order literally everything on the food menu, the drinks list is where the wheat is, which is the reverse of every other record here. Second: the FROZEN RETAIL products sold in-store and online are NOT held to the dine-in 五葷 rule and may contain garlic — so the packet you buy on the way out is not governed by the policy that governs the plate you just ate. ⚠ ON HALAL: no pork and no alcohol in any dish, but alcohol IS used to sanitise equipment and tableware, and the seasonings are not halal-certified; the shop asks customers to judge for themselves rather than claiming certification. ⚠ RECORD-LEVEL NOTE FOR THE HUMAN GATE: on this evidence the tier fields for this shop are probably understated, but an upgrade of gf_confidence or vegan_status is a human decision under the asymmetry rule and is not made here. The published menu sections are Morning, Lunch, Dinner and Kids; re-check if the shop ever publishes the menu as text.

tokyo_shibuya_wagyu_yakiniku_u.price_note: Prices 税込, from the shop's own site (渋谷区道玄坂2-3-1 渋谷駅前ビル 4F — the record's Dogenzaka placement). ⚠ AT A YAKINIKU HOUSE THE MEAT IS NOT THE PROBLEM AND THE DIPPING SAUCE IS. Nothing on this card's grill sections is breaded and the shop buys whole animals, so the raw material is clean — but yakiniku is eaten dipped in a soy-based tare, and this shop marks which items come 塩 or 味噌 and which do not. That labelling is the useful part: 上タン塩, タン塩, 白ホルモン（塩・味噌）, 和牛ハツ焼き（塩・味噌）, ねぎ塩ハラミ and ごま油香るにんにくオイル焼き all name a salt or oil finish, while タン赤身のたれ焼き names the tare outright. The 味噌 option is not the safe one — Japanese yakiniku miso tare is cut with soy sauce. ⚠ The shop sells a 「タン専用ねぎ塩だれ」 at ¥290 as a separate purchase, which means the default is not automatically that sauce; ask what arrives. ⚠ THE COOKED SECTIONS ARE WHERE THE WHEAT IS: 石焼ビビンバ and both 和牛ビビンバ are gochujang-dressed (Korean gochujang is conventionally made with wheat flour); コムタンスープ and ユッケジャンスープ can be ordered ご飯 or UDON, which is wheat; both 冷麺 and the 坦々冷麺 are Korean cold noodles whose Japanese-market versions frequently contain wheat flour; and 韓国海苔 is sesame-oiled seaweed that sometimes carries a soy seasoning. ⚠ VEGAN: the 焼き野菜 section is genuinely all-plant — courgette, onion, king oyster mushroom, asparagus, pumpkin, and a garlic-in-sesame-oil grill at ¥590 each — and the ナムル盛り合わせ is four seasoned vegetables. Both go on a grill shared with beef, and namul dressings sometimes carry fish seasoning.

tokyo_okome_to_gohan_sumidaya_.price_note: No menu and no prices are published anywhere on this shop's own web presence, so this is an honest empty rather than an unfinished one. ⚠ THE URL ON THE RECORD IS DEAD. The record cites https://shop.sumidaya.jp/ ; that host's TLS certificate expired on 2025-12-20 (GlobalSign AlphaSSL, issued 2025-11-17), so every browser will refuse it outright, and ignoring the certificate only reaches a 404. The online store the record was pointing at is gone. The live site is the apex, https://sumidaya.jp/ , and the record's website field should be repointed there. ⚠ WHAT THE LIVE SITE DOES CONFIRM about the Asakusa shop: 〒111-0033 東京都台東区花川戸2-13-9 マルイシ浅草1階, tel 03-5830-3285, open 10:00–17:00, 不定休 (irregular closing days — there is no fixed rest day to plan around). A five-hour daytime window with no published rest day is the practical fact a visitor needs, and the record does not carry it. ⚠ THE ONIGIRI CLAIM NEEDS CARE. The record calls this an onigiri specialist. Sumidaya's own site documents an early-morning omusubi counter (早朝おむすび販売 08:45〜10:00) at its MACHIDAI HILLS branch, not at Asakusa; for Asakusa the site says only 「お米とごはん」 and lists no products at all. Whether Asakusa sells made-up onigiri, cooked rice by weight, or raw rice is not stated first-party. ⚠ WHAT THE COMPANY DOES DOCUMENT is milling, not cooking: a 五つ星お米マイスター blends selected brown rices, and the house 古式精米製法 (a registered trademark) mills them on an inherited large recirculating mill for roughly seven times as long as ordinary milling. Plain Japanese white rice is naturally free of both gluten and animal products, so the raw material here is about as safe as Japanese food gets — but nothing about fillings, furikake, seasoning, nori or shared equipment is published, and those are where onigiri stops being safe. Ask in person. The shop links a Tabelog reservation page (opened 2026-06-19) and an Uber Eats storefront; the Uber Eats link is the only place a priced list is likely to exist, and it did not serve to this egress.

tokyo_raamen_hayashida_shinjuk.price_note: The operator's own site (INGS, which runs はやし田 along with 鳳仙花, 鈴蘭, くろ渦, ふじ松 and others) publishes NO menu and NO prices for any branch — it is a brand-and-branch-list site only. So no priced items could be recorded. ⚠ BUT THE SITE MAKES TWO FIRST-PARTY INGREDIENT STATEMENTS THAT SETTLE THE DIET QUESTION, and they are worth more here than a price list. On the noodles: 「麺は数種類の厳選小麦を絶妙なバランスで配合し、コシ、のど越し、風味を高次元でバランスさせた逸品です」 — the noodle is an explicit blend of SEVERAL SELECTED WHEATS. This is not an inference from the word ラーメン; the shop says wheat, in its own voice. There is no rice-noodle or gluten-free option mentioned anywhere on the site. On the broth: 「鴨と大山どりの丸鶏を惜しげもなく使用し、炊き上げ」 — duck plus whole Daisen chickens, boiled down. Both animal. Nothing on the site is vegan or could be made so. ⚠ BRANCH CONFIRMED: 新宿店 is 〒160-0022 東京都新宿区新宿3-31-5 新宿ペガサス館102, 03-6380-0047, 11:00〜23:00, 無休, three minutes from JR Shinjuku east exit — this matches the record's placement. Note that several sibling branches carry a 「スープ切れ早仕舞いあり」 warning (may close early when the broth runs out); the Shinjuku entry does not, but at a shop of this style it is still worth arriving before the end of service.

tokyo_magari_curry_shimokawa_s.price_note: ⚠ THE URL ON THE RECORD IS NOT A RESTAURANT MENU — IT IS A MERCHANDISE SHOP. high007.thebase.in sells exactly three things: a ~50-page self-published zine about the owner's curry recipes (¥2,200 incl. postage) and two butter-chicken spice kits (¥900 for one, ¥4,000 for five), both currently SOLD OUT. No dish served at the counter, and no price for one, appears anywhere on it. ⚠ MORE IMPORTANTLY, THIS IS NOT A RESTAURANT WITH A FIXED ADDRESS, AND THE RECORD READS AS THOUGH IT IS. 間借りカレー means the cook rents somebody else's kitchen and premises for a shift. The shop states its own model plainly: 「新宿を中心に間借りカレー屋を営業しながら海外や日本全国でもイベントをしております」 — a roving pop-up based around Shinjuku that also runs events elsewhere in Japan and overseas — and its trading hours are stated as 営業時間：不定期 (irregular). The operator is 下川晃弘; the address in the legal notice is BASE Inc.'s Roppongi head office, i.e. the platform's, not a place you can eat. Anyone travelling to a pin for this shop can arrive to find no such restaurant. Check Instagram for the current host venue before going. This is the single most important thing about the record and it is not currently on it. ⚠ WHAT THE ZINE'S CONTENTS PAGE DOES REVEAL about the repertoire, since nothing else does: butter chicken, pork vindaloo, a sashimi-herb curry, beef-tongue rendang, an original nasi lemak, peanut curry mee, sambal ikan bilis, and a documented VEGETABLE-CURRY line built on house onion-koji and tomato-koji with a 重ね煮 base, worked into a sambal and a rasam. So a plant-based curry genuinely exists in this cook's repertoire — but sambal ikan bilis is dried anchovy, and whether the koji is rice-koji (gluten-free) or barley-koji is not stated. Both are questions for the day. The spice kit's own ingredient list includes 生乳 (milk) and cashew.

tokyo_rasera_aomori_kyodo_ryor.price_note: ⚠ THE URL ON THE RECORD IS DEAD AT THE DNS LEVEL. The record cites https://lacela.net/ ; that name now returns SERVFAIL from public resolvers — it does not resolve at all, so no browser can reach it and no amount of retrying will help. The shop's live official site is https://lacela0408.com/ and the record's website field should be repointed there. The record's menu_url also points at a Tabelog dtlmenu page, which this egress cannot read; the prices below come from the shop's own site instead and supersede it. ⚠ ADDRESS CONFIRMED against the live site: 〒150-0043 東京都渋谷区道玄坂1-20-12 MT道玄坂 地下1階, tel 03-3770-7522 — this matches the record. Some aggregators file the shop under 渋谷マークシティ; that is the landmark, not the address. ⚠ HOW FRESH THIS IS: the new site's own blog stops at 2024-09, and its コース page still carries unedited placeholder text (「これはダミーテキストです」) beside the real course description — the rebuild was never finished. The 料理 page itself is fully populated with real dishes and real prices and is the best first-party source that exists, but treat the prices as roughly two years old and confirm on the night. ⚠ THE GLUTEN PICTURE IS UNIFORMLY BAD AND THE RECORD IS RIGHT ABOUT IT. The house course is built on せんべい汁, whose defining ingredient is 南部せんべい — a WHEAT-flour cracker simmered in the broth. That is not a trace risk, it is the dish. Beyond it, 長芋の醤油漬け is steeped in soy sauce, いか餃子 has a wheat wrapper, 十和田バラ焼き and シャモロック山賊焼き are soy-glazed, ねぶた漬け is a soy-and-kelp pickle, and both カレー and 親子丼 carry roux or soy. Nothing here is wheat-free and the shop offers no gluten-free anything. ⚠ VEGAN: also uniformly no. Even the vegetable-sounding items lean on animal ingredients — 貝焼き味噌 is miso simmered in a scallop shell with egg, 梅水晶 is shark cartilage, ポテサラ has mayonnaise, and the dashi under the nabe and simmered dishes is bonito. もろきゅう, 梅きゅう, 冷やしトマト and ぱりぱり塩こんぶキャベツ are the only plausibly plant-only plates on the card, and each still turns on the miso or the seasoning used — ask. The plain rice portions are the one unambiguous safe order.

items.en: Senbei-jiru course — 7+ dishes with 2h all-you-can-drink Aomori sake
items.note: ⚠ The centrepiece せんべい汁 is a hot pot in which 南部せんべい — a WHEAT-flour cracker — is simmered until it softens. Wheat is the point of the dish, not a contaminant. The course also includes 揚げ物 (fried, so wheat batter) and しばれ生ハムのサラダ (cured pork). Stated contents: 前菜, 自家製にんにく味噌のポテトサラダ, しばれ生ハムのサラダ, 揚げ物, せんべい汁, 雑炊, デザート.

One of the very few plates here that could be plant-only. The cucumber is; the もろみ味噌 is the question — moromi miso is frequently built on a BARLEY koji, and barley carries no labelling duty in Japan. Some versions also add bonito. Ask on both counts.

Cucumber and umeboshi are both plant and wheat-free in the plain form, making this and the chilled tomato the best bets on the card for either diet. Bought-in ume paste is often let down with dashi or bonito flakes — ask.

Cured pork — しばれる is Tohoku dialect for a hard freeze. The same ham appears inside the senbei-jiru course.

The Towada beef-and-onion dish served as a rice bowl. Sweet soy sauce.

Japanese curry is thickened with a WHEAT-FLOUR roux, and commercial roux blocks contain both wheat and animal fat as standard. Assume neither diet — the shop makes no claim to building its curry from spices.

Plain steamed white rice sold as a bare portion — no tare, dashi or mix-ins are listed, unlike every other item in this section. Japanese short-grain rice contains no gluten and no animal product. The realistic caveat is a shared serving scoop in a kitchen frying tempura all evening: fine for an intolerance, worth a word for coeliac disease.

tokyo_kameya_shinjuku_ten_kame.price_note: The only menu that exists for this shop online is the two-line 「当店のおすすめ」 card the 新宿西口商店街振興組合 (the Omoide Yokocho traders' association) publishes for its member shops. That is the association writing about a member, not the shop writing about itself, so this is marked partial rather than authoritative — and the association stamps the page 「2021年3月時点の情報です」. ⚠ THOSE PRICES ARE OVER FIVE YEARS OLD AND WILL BE WRONG. Japanese standing-soba prices rose materially across 2022–2024; treat ¥380/¥430 as the shape of the menu (this is a cheap standing shop) rather than as what you will pay. ⚠ WHAT IS WORTH KNOWING BESIDES THE FOOD: 24-hour operation, CLOSED SUNDAYS, CASH ONLY, and eight seats — a 24-hour shop that shuts one whole day a week and takes no cards is an easy trip to waste. 東京都新宿区西新宿1-2-10, 03-3344-3820. ⚠ DIET: this is one of the clearest no-go shops in the dataset for coeliac visitors, and it is worth being blunt about why. Cheap Tokyo tachigui soba is typically a 二八 blend or weaker — more wheat flour than buckwheat by the time it is priced this low — the tsuyu is a wheat-brewed soy sauce and bonito dashi, and the headline dish is topped with deep-fried tempura in a wheat batter dropped into oil shared with everything else on the counter. There is no dish here without wheat and no dashi here without fish. Nothing on this menu works for either diet.

items.en: The original ten-tama soba — soba with tempura and a hot-spring egg
items.note: The shop's signature and the reason it is known. Wheat arrives three ways at once: the soba itself (a cheap tachigui blend is mostly wheat flour), the tempura's batter, and the wheat-brewed soy sauce in the tsuyu. The tsuyu is also bonito dashi and there is a whole egg on top, so it fails vegan on two counts before the broth is considered.
The same bowl without the egg. Still wheat in the noodle, the batter and the tsuyu, and still a bonito-and-soy broth. The fryer is shared.

tokyo_sugoi_niboshi_ramen_nagi.price_note: ⚠ NO PRICES EXIST FIRST-PARTY. Nagi Spirits' corporate site carries an お品書き page that names and describes the group's dishes but prints no price against any of them, and the branch page for this shop carries none either. The two items below are therefore recorded without prices — the dish identities and their ingredients are solid, the cost is not known. Marked partial for that reason. ⚠ WHICH DISHES APPLY HERE. The corporate menu page covers BOTH of Nagi's brands — the 煮干 (niboshi) line and the BUTAO tonkotsu line, whose 黄・赤・黒・翠 kings belong to the Butao shops. Nagi's own branch list tags this address 「煮干」, so only the two niboshi dishes below are this shop's menu; a visitor should not arrive expecting to order Akao or Kuroo here. ⚠ SHOP FACTS CONFIRMED FIRST-PARTY: 東京都新宿区歌舞伎町1-1-10 2F, inside 新宿ゴールデン街 (the English page places it on G2 street); 03-3205-1925; OPEN 24 HOURS; ten seats at an L-shaped counter. This is Nagi's founding shop — 「新宿ゴールデン街からはじまった、ラーメン凪の創業店です」 — and a Tabelog Ramen Hyakumeiten 2017 winner. Ten seats in Golden Gai at any hour means queueing. ⚠ DIET, IN SHORT: nothing here works for either. The shop's whole identity is dried sardine — it states it buys over five tonnes of niboshi a month and blends more than twenty varieties into the broth — so the soup is a fish product by design, not by accident, and no vegetable version is offered. The noodles are wheat. There is no gluten-free or plant-based option anywhere in the group.

tokyo_koshitsu_izakaya_banya_n.price_note: From the shop's own branch page. Every price below is given twice by the shop: the standard price and the lower 「番屋公式サイト限定価格」 you get by booking through the official site rather than a reservation portal — a real ¥500 saving per head on most courses, and the shop states the same discount applies to telephone bookings. All courses are two-hour all-you-can-drink. Branch: 個室居酒屋番屋 西新宿住友ビル店, 03-5381-5757, five minutes from Shinjuku station, ALL SEATING IS PRIVATE ROOMS (10 sunken-kotatsu rooms and 15 table rooms, 2 to 80 people), open Sundays and public holidays. ⚠ THIS SHOP PUBLISHES AN EXPLICIT VEGETARIAN COURSE AND THAT IS THE HEADLINE HERE. 「ベジタリアンコース」, ¥6,500 (¥6,000 booked direct), described by the shop as 「お肉やお魚、乳製品を使用していない、お豆腐・お野菜中心のコース」 — no meat, no fish, NO DAIRY, tofu- and vegetable-centred. The shop says the listed contents are one example and invites you to discuss budget and content, and asks you to write the request in the booking form's notes field. For a large-format banquet izakaya to carry a standing no-meat-no-fish-no-dairy banquet course at all is unusual and genuinely useful for a mixed group. ⚠ BUT DO NOT READ IT AS VEGAN WITHOUT ASKING ABOUT THE DASHI, AND THE SHOP'S OWN SITE IS WHY. The vegetarian course leads with 水菜の煮びたし (a simmered-and-steeped dish), 豆腐と茄子のあんかけ (a thickened sauce) and 冷やしきつねうどん (a noodle broth) — three dishes that in a Japanese kitchen are built on dashi. On the very same site the shop describes its house 黄金出汁 as 「二種類の鰹節と昆布をたっぷりと使い」 — two kinds of BONITO plus kelp. So the standing house dashi is a fish stock. The shop's claim is that the course uses no fish; that would require a separate kombu dashi, which the shop does not say it makes. Ask this specific question when booking. ⚠ THERE IS NO GLUTEN-FREE COURSE HERE AT ALL, INCLUDING THE VEGETARIAN ONE. Every single course on this page, without exception, contains a 揚げ物 course (tempura — wheat batter) AND an 食事 course that is either udon, a soy-dressed noodle or sushi. The vegetarian course is no different: it has アスパラ・しいたけ・しし唐の天婦羅 and 冷やしきつねうどん. A coeliac visitor cannot eat any course at this restaurant as written. ⚠ AND THE SHOP SAYS SO ITSELF, IN UNUSUALLY DIRECT LANGUAGE. Its allergy notice reads: 「当店では調理環境の都合上、完全なアレルギー対応は致しかねます。微量混入を完全に防ぐことはできず、重篤なアレルギーをお持ちのお客様のご利用をお断りする場合がございます」 — it cannot fully accommodate allergies, cannot prevent trace contamination, AND MAY DECLINE TO SERVE CUSTOMERS WITH SEVERE ALLERGIES. It goes on to place the final decision and all responsibility on the diner and their doctor. That is a shop being honest rather than a shop being careless, but a severely allergic traveller should take it at its word and telephone before booking, not turn up. ⚠ Course contents change with supply (「入荷状況により、お料理内容を変更させて頂く場合がございます」) and some courses are 数量限定. Several are seasonal — the 冷しゃぶ course is dated from 1 July and the 夏野菜 course is a summer card — so expect the line-up to rotate.

items.en: Vegetarian course — 8 dishes, 2h all-you-can-drink; no meat, fish or dairy
items.section: ベジタリアンコース (vegetarian course)
items.note: ⚠ The one course here built for a non-meat eater, and the shop states it uses no meat, no fish and no dairy. Contents: 水菜の煮びたし / アボカド刺し・湯葉刺し / 野菜の蒸し陶板 / 豆腐と茄子のあんかけ / ミックスビーンズとアボカドのサラダ 胡麻ドレッシング / アスパラ・しいたけ・しし唐の天婦羅 / 冷やしきつねうどん / 大豆アイスクリーム — note the soy ice cream rather than dairy, which shows the no-dairy claim is being taken seriously. GF is a flat NO: the tempura is wheat-battered and the kitsune udon is wheat, both written into the course. VEGAN is 'ask' rather than 'vegan' for one specific reason — 煮びたし, あんかけ and うどんつゆ are dashi dishes, and this shop's own house dashi is documented on the same website as two kinds of bonito with kelp. Ask whether these three are made with a separate kombu dashi. The shop says content is flexible and asks you to note requests when booking, so this is a question it expects.

tokyo_aogashimaya.price_note: ⚠ THE MENU BELOW IS USER-SUBMITTED, NOT THE SHOP’S OWN BOARD, AND THAT IS THE FIRST THING TO KNOW ABOUT IT. Yahoo! Map heads this list ユーザー投稿のメニュー — items photographed and typed in by members of the public — and prints its own disclaimer, ※ 掲載時点の情報です。最新情報は店舗でご確認ください. Nothing here is dated. Some entries are visibly other diners’ shorthand rather than menu lines. It is recorded because it is the only itemised, priced list that exists for this shop on any page reachable from here, and because the dish names themselves are informative; treat every figure as approximate and every spelling as a diner’s. Gnavi was read and shows two dishes with photographs — 刺身盛合せ and 和風サラダ — and no prices at all. Hitosara was read and shows no menu, only an average dinner spend of 5,000〜5,999円, which is a long way above the two prices below and suggests the real bill here is built from courses and island shochu rather than from the à la carte plates that diners happened to photograph. Instagram is the shop’s only channel and serves a login wall to this egress; Tabelog has served HTTP 403 to this egress since 2026-09-02. ⚠ WHAT THIS SHOP ACTUALLY IS, because the name will mean nothing to most people: Aogashima is an inhabited volcanic island roughly 360km south of Tokyo, administratively part of the metropolis, population under 200, reachable only by helicopter or a boat that frequently cannot land. This izakaya cooks that island’s food in Nishi-Shinjuku. That is why 明日葉 (ashitaba) heads the list — it is the island green, a hardy herbaceous plant that grows across the Izu islands and is eaten as a vegetable there. ⚠ AND WHY THE ONE VEGETABLE DISH ON THE LIST IS NOT A VEGETABLE DISH: 明日葉のツナマヨ和え is ashitaba dressed with TUNA AND MAYONNAISE. The island green, the thing a plant-eater would order on sight, arrives bound in fish and egg. Nothing published for this shop is meat-free.

items.ja: 明日葉のツナマヨ和え
items.en: Ashitaba dressed with tuna and mayonnaise — ashitaba is the Izu-islands green the shop is here to serve, a bitter, celery-scented herb that regrows so fast it is named “tomorrow’s leaf”

items.note: 明日葉は伊豆諸島の島野菜。ただしツナ＝魚、マヨ＝卵。The green is the island; the dressing is not. Gluten: Japanese mayonnaise is egg, oil and vinegar and normally carries no wheat, but an 和え dressing at an izakaya commonly gets a splash of soy — ask.

tokyo_menya_nukaji.price_note: ⚠ THIN RECORD, AND THE THINNESS IS THE FINDING. Tabelog publishes exactly ONE item for this shop — 味玉ラーメン at 830円 — with no 更新日 and no other line, so what follows is one dish from a counter that plainly sells more than one dish. The entry is filed so nobody re-researches it from scratch, not because the menu is now known. THE DIETARY ANSWER IS NONETHELESS FIRM, because it does not depend on the missing items: ramen noodles are WHEAT and are made with かん水 (alkaline salts), there is no rice-noodle version anywhere in the tsukemen idiom, and 味玉 is an egg marinated in a soy-and-mirin bath, which is wheat again. A coeliac has nothing here and a vegan has nothing here, and no unlisted item is likely to change that at a tsukemen counter. The shop is recorded as ラーメン/つけ麺 with an 8-seat counter in Udagawachō, open 11:00–17:00 and closed Sundays — daytime only, which for Shibuya is unusual and worth planning around. Average spend 1,000–1,999円.

The broth is undeclared; at a tsukemen shop it is conventionally pork and/or chicken with fish powder. Nothing here for a coeliac or a vegan.
